question: Two trains having lengths of 240 m and 410 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 110 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 240 + 410 = 650 m

Relative speed (same direction) = 110 − 80 = 30 km/h = 30 × 5/18 = 25/3 m/s

Time = 650 ÷ (25/3) = 650 × 3 / 25 = 78 seconds

Time in minutes = 78 ÷ 60 = 1.3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 1.3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of slower train = 240 m

Length of faster train = 410 m

Speed of slower train = 80 km/h

Speed of faster train = 110 km/h
